author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Woonsocket drivers face a coordinated series of bridge changes Friday evening as one crossing reopens and two others close for rehabilitation, according to the Rhode Island Department of Transportation.

The Singleton Street Bridge, closed since early June, is scheduled to reopen. Nearby, the Wood Avenue Bridge will close for about six weeks and the River Street Bridge will close through the end of 2026. Both carry local traffic across waterways near major neighborhood intersections.

Wood Avenue traffic will be detoured along Mill Street, Social Street and Diamond Hill Road. The River Street detour uses River Street, Singleton Street, Harris Avenue and Blackstone Street for cars and pedestrians. Trucks will follow a longer route through Blackstone and Millville, Massachusetts, before returning through North Smithfield.

The changes are part of two projects representing a combined $41.8 million investment. RIDOT coordinated the Singleton reopening with the River Street closure to reduce overlapping disruption. All dates remain subject to weather and construction conditions, and drivers should follow posted detour signs.
dek: Singleton Street Bridge is set to reopen while Wood Avenue and River Street bridges close for rehabilitation.
headline: Woonsocket bridge closures and reopening reshape Friday travel
